title: Rapper: A Parameter-Aware Repair-in-Memory Accelerator for Blockchain Storage Platform
problem: Blockchain storage nodes go offline unpredictably, causing data loss. Data repair processes rely on time-consuming erasure coding algorithms dominated by vector-matrix multiplications.
motivation: Blockchain storage platforms need efficient data repair to recover from node failures and prevent data loss.
method: Rapper speeds up data repair for blockchain storage by organizing ReRAM (a type of computer memory that stores data without needing power) into specific hardware structures—double bank, XRU, XGroup, and crossbar—that allow many calculations to run simultaneously. Instead of doing repair calculations one at a time, Rapper performs multiple calculations in parallel using these hardware structures. It also automatically adjusts how it schedules the repair work based on the size of data chunks being repaired.
key_novelty: Rapper accelerates blockchain data repair by running the repair calculations directly in ReRAM (a type of computer memory that stores data without power), automatically adapting to different data chunk sizes.
contributions: Double bank XRU XGroup ReRAM crossbar hardware architecture for parallel repair operations
Parallel decoding/encoding strategy to fully exploit ReRAM internal parallelism
Adaptive parameter-aware mapping for variable stripe sizes
1.96× speedup demonstration on Storj blockchain storage platform
primary_theme: In-memory accelerator for blockchain data repair
